text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mother and two children killed by bomb in south Lebanon.
- Israel plans to test new Scud missile interceptor.
- Troops will be used to quell opposition.
- Egypt and Lebanon sign trade deal.
- Central bank governor determined to push through bank reforms aimed at capital increases.
- Interior minister speeds up security measures.
The government has said it would crack down on a civil disobedience campaign led by former Hizbollah leader Sheikh Sobhi Tufaili.
- Five killed and seven injured in an escalation of violence in south Lebanon.
- Christian Maronite Patriarch Cardinal Nasrallah Sfeir says "No peace in Lebanon without comprehensive peace in the region".
- The army will soon take measures against those moving against the state's authority.
- Lebanon's foreign minister says Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is exporting his domestic problems and anything is possible in south Lebanon.
South Lebanon this week witnesssed the worst violence since an Israeli offensive more than a year ago. Thirteen people were killed.
